reuse.why: All four steps land in the existing getScheduledAmount, reuse getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance, and the API field and budget templates (which had an inline midpoint) are routed through it.

duplication.why: Removes the inline midpoint copy in schedule-template.ts and adds no new copies; the expected-amount rule exists once.

placement.why: The rule is in shared/schedules.ts and the API field in scheduleModel.toExternal, but passing the op into the helper also used by display cells pushes the planning rule into UI display.

scope.why: Beyond planning, API and posting paths it changes UI display/search values (SchedulesTable amount cell, mobile list item and filters), which no step asked for.

maintainability.why: A single small helper with tests is easy to own; the op parameter inserted before the positional inverse flag and the mixing of nominal and planning amounts in one function are the remaining warts.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains the amount operator (the real variation) and one isapprox branch; every consumer, including schedule-template and the new API field, calls it.
